Create a Complete UNO Deck

create_uno_deck.Rd

Constructs a full UNO card deck consisting of 108 cards, following official game rules. The function generates all standard components: number cards (0–9), action cards (Skip, Reverse, +2), and wild cards (Wild, Wild Draw 4). This is the foundational step in setting up a UNO game simulation.

Usage

create_uno_deck()

Value

A tibble (data frame) with exactly 108 rows and 3 columns:

  • color – Character. Card color: one of "red", "green", "blue", "yellow", or "wild"

  • value – Character. Either a number (as string), action (e.g. "reverse"), or wild type

  • type – Character. Card type: one of "number", "action", or "wild"

Details

For each of the four main colors (red, green, blue, yellow), the deck includes:

  • One copy of the number card 0

  • Two copies of each number card from 1 to 9

  • Two copies of each action card: "skip", "reverse", and "+2"

In addition to the color-specific cards, the deck contains:

  • Four "wild" cards

  • Four "wild_draw4" cards

The resulting deck is sorted by color, card type, and value for readability and is ready for dealing via deal_hands or gameplay via play_game.

The UNO deck is generated using a data frame expansion approach powered by expand_grid() and dplyr tools. Number cards are replicated using a conditional multiplier to meet UNO rules.
This function is designed to be reproducible and efficient for simulations and testing.
It returns a tibble suitable for direct use in the deal_hands function or shuffling workflows.

Examples

# Generate the full UNO deck
deck <- create_uno_deck()
#> Error in expand_grid(color = colors, value = as.character(numbers)) %>%     mutate(type = "number") %>% group_by(value) %>% mutate(replication = if_else(value ==     "0", 1, 2)) %>% ungroup() %>% slice(rep(1:n(), replication)) %>%     select(-replication): could not find function "%>%"

# Check number of cards
nrow(deck)  # Should return 108
#> Error: object 'deck' not found

# Summary by type
table(deck$type)
#> Error: object 'deck' not found

# Check unique card colors
unique(deck$color)
#> Error: object 'deck' not found

# Preview the first few rows
head(deck)
#> Error: object 'deck' not found

# Use with deal_hands()
dealt <- deal_hands(deck, n_players = 4)
#> Error: object 'deck' not found
lapply(dealt$hands, head)
#> Error: object 'dealt' not found
